payload.name: Per-person searches for multi-person activity questions
payload.description: When a question asks what ways, methods, or items multiple people use for an activity, run a separate search for each named person before answering.
content: When a question asks for the ways, methods, or items two or more people use for an activity (e.g., enhance, improve, enjoy their practice), do not rely only on a single joint query with all names. Run at least one hybrid search per person, combining that person's name with the activity and preference-oriented terms such as 'prefers', 'uses', 'likes', 'enjoys', 'enhances'.

Include 'preference' and 'event' memory kinds in these per-person searches, since relevant details are often stored as individual preferences or purchase/use events that do not mention the other person.

Before answering, verify that each named person has at least one retrieved memory about the activity and its enhancement; if not, issue an additional targeted search for that person before finalizing the answer.

solves: Joint multi-person queries about an activity can miss person-specific preference and event memories, causing answers to omit one person's methods. This rule applies when a question asks for the ways, methods, or items multiple people use for a shared activity: run a separate search for each person to surface evidence stored individually. It does not apply to single-person activity questions or to recommendation-from-one-person questions.
